subsystems.name: Field generator array
subsystems.role: creates the acoustic or magnetic field that holds and shapes the medium.
parts: drive electronics with phase and amplitude control

subsystems.name: Responsive medium
subsystems.role: the material that temporarily takes the shape dictated by the field.
parts: optional binder or coating for cohesion

subsystems.name: Computational engine
subsystems.role: converts a desired digital shape into the field pattern that produces it.
parts: inverse solver for acoustic or magnetic fields

subsystems.name: Interaction sensing
subsystems.role: tracks the user's hands or tools so the shape can respond and update.

subsystems.name: Containment and safety
subsystems.role: keeps the medium, sound or magnetic fields safely enclosed.
parts: sealed chamber for particles or fluid

buildSteps.title: Choose the medium and actuation principle
buildSteps.detail: Decide between acoustic levitation of lightweight particles and magnetic shaping of ferrofluid, based on desired resolution, speed and safety.

buildSteps.title: Design the array
buildSteps.detail: Arrange transducers or coils in a 2D or 3D grid, spacing them so their fields overlap to form a controllable trap or shape.

buildSteps.title: Build drive electronics
buildSteps.detail: Create circuits that can set the phase and amplitude of each array element independently, at frequencies from tens of kilohertz (acoustic) to kilohertz (magnetic).

buildSteps.title: Implement the inverse solver
buildSteps.detail: Write software that takes a target shape and computes the field pattern needed to assemble the medium into that shape, using iterative optimisation.

buildSteps.title: Calibrate with static shapes
buildSteps.detail: Test simple forms like lines, dots and surfaces, measuring how closely the medium follows the computed field.

buildSteps.title: Add real-time sensing and feedback
buildSteps.detail: Integrate cameras or sensors to detect user touch, then update the field at least 30 times per second so the shape feels responsive.

buildSteps.title: Scale resolution and refresh rate
buildSteps.detail: Increase array density, improve solver speed and reduce latency to allow finer, more dynamic shapes.

prerequisites.why: standing ultrasonic waves can trap and move small particles in mid-air, demonstrated in laboratory setups.
magnetic fields can sculpt ferrofluid into spikes and blobs, but not yet into arbitrary high-resolution shapes.
grids of coils with independent control are used in magnetic levitation and haptics research.
computing the exact field to form a complex shape fast enough for interaction is still a research challenge.
detecting where and how a user touches a dynamic shape requires dense, low-latency sensing.

prerequisites.tech: Safe containment of particles or fluid
prerequisites.why: keeping airborne particles or magnetic fluid fully enclosed while allowing open interaction is unsolved.

pathway.milestone: laboratory demonstrations of levitated particles and ferrofluid shapes
pathway.unlocks: proof that fields can assemble matter into simple temporary forms.

pathway.milestone: interactive prototypes with centimetre-scale resolution and real-time response
pathway.unlocks: tactile feedback for simple digital objects, like buttons or raised lines.

pathway.milestone: integration with virtual and augmented reality headsets
pathway.unlocks: feeling virtual objects without wearing gloves or holding controllers.

pathway.milestone: general-purpose matter-to-data interfaces with millimetre resolution and fast refresh
pathway.unlocks: physical telepresence, where remote data becomes touchable shapes in real time.
